title: Seminar on artificial intelligence applied to breast cancer
content_html:
Diverso Lab is holding a new Outreach Seminar titled "A retrospective on the 'Para-Dis-Verso': some results and many challenges", which will take place on Monday, 15 June 2026, at 12:30, in Room A2.11.

The session will be led by Jorge García Gutiérrez and will address the challenges of domain generalisation in breast cancer molecular classification using foundation models, based on a cross-cohort exploratory study (Domain generalisation challenges in breast cancer molecular classification using foundation models: a cross-cohort exploratory study).


The seminar will cover topics such as the role of foundation models in healthcare, domain generalisation, breast cancer molecular classification, and the current challenges and upcoming opportunities within this line of research, which brings together digital pathology, artificial intelligence and multi-cohort studies with a common goal, to improve classification and, with it, patient care.

Under the motto "Researching today, transforming tomorrow", this initiative reflects Diverso Lab's commitment to science, artificial intelligence and health as a team effort aimed at generating real impact.

title: SensOlive Project: Showcasing the Future of Smart Irrigation
content_html:
Recently, our team had the pleasure of hosting a presentation event to share the latest results of the SensOlive project with local farmers and our collaborative partners from IRNAS, CSIC, ig4, and Diversolab. It was a fantastic opportunity to demonstrate how we are bringing the second modernization of Andalusian irrigation to life through the application of artificial intelligence.

Field Visit to La Hampa

The event kicked off with a hands-on visit to the La Hampa experimental farm, located in Coria del Río. Here, we walked attendees through the physical setup of the project, showcasing the actual sensors—such as dendrometers—used to monitor the trees in the field.

La Hampa, managed by IRNAS-CSIC, has been an instrumental testing ground for our research. Since 2021, we have been running continuous trials on Manzanilla olive hedgerows to fine-tune irrigation and nutrient management, even testing stronger water stress levels to gather robust, actionable data.

From Physical Sensors to Digital Twins

Following the field tour, the focus shifted from the soil to the screen, exploring the digital transformation driving SensOlive.

  • Data Management: Our partners at ig4 demonstrated their platform, which is designed to seamlessly manage and process the complex data generated by the physical field sensors.

  • Intelligent Digital Twins: The team from Diversolab then presented the SensOlive web application, highlighting its core added value: the integration of intelligent digital twins.

This technology is at the heart of SensOlive's innovation. By leveraging IoT, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and geospatial analysis, the project is developing "virtual sensors". This breakthrough allows us to infer accurate field data and apply water optimization models to similar agricultural plots with minimal physical installation or maintenance required from the farmer.

Maximizing Savings in Times of Scarcity

The ultimate goal of SensOlive is to tackle the pressing challenges posed by climate change and increasingly frequent adverse water cycles. By utilizing these advanced technologies to maximize water savings during shortages—particularly in complex ecological production systems—we aim to ensure both environmental sustainability and economic profitability for the agricultural sector.

Funding and Institutional Support

The SensOlive project (Reference: PLSQ 00162) is co-financed by the European Union and the Junta de Andalucía. This initiative is part of the "Europe invests in rural areas" effort, promoting innovation and efficiency in our agricultural systems.

     

We want to extend a huge thank you to all the farmers who attended, as well as our project partners—Universidad de Sevilla, IRNAS-CSIC, ig4 agronomía, and DIVERSO LAB—for making this event a success. Together, we are building a more resilient future for our rural areas.
